name: Mechanics: motion and force
description: Units, vectors, motion, forces, energy, momentum and rotation, taught at the Kepler outpost.
about:
Mechanics realm ("Mechanics: motion and force"): units, vectors, motion, forces, energy, momentum and rotation, for an
adult who has finished Foundations and Calculus 1 and nothing more. Same Kepler outpost, now building and launching its own
machines at the Proving Ground on the ridge. Mira is still the mentor. The concept plan is docs/plans/MECH-PLAN.md.

chapters.name: Measures and arrows
chapters.blurb: Units, powers of ten, vectors and their parts, and the first look at motion.

sector.name: Survey Office
sector.purpose: measure everything in one agreed set of units

chapters.name: Motion on a line
chapters.blurb: Velocity and acceleration as derivatives, constant acceleration and free fall.

sector.name: Sled Run
sector.purpose: predict where a sled will be at any moment

chapters.name: Motion in a plane
chapters.blurb: Projectiles, motion in circles and how motion looks from a moving rover.

sector.name: Catapult Field
sector.purpose: land a supply pod exactly where it is needed

chapters.name: Forces
chapters.blurb: Newton’s laws, weight, tension, ramps and friction.

sector.name: Crane Yard
sector.purpose: lift and haul loads without snapping a cable

chapters.name: Work and power
chapters.blurb: Forces that turn, air that drags, and the work and power a machine delivers.

sector.name: Engine Hall
sector.purpose: know how much energy each machine needs

chapters.name: Energy and momentum
chapters.blurb: Stored energy, energy that is kept, collisions and the centre of mass.

chapters.name: Spin and orbit

sector.name: Flywheel Vault
sector.purpose: keep the flywheels and satellites turning

mentor.name: Mira
mentor.opening: I’m Mira. Every machine on the ridge obeys a few simple rules, and we have to {purpose}. Your task is “{title}.” {brief} The idea we need: {topic}.
mentor.closing: You already have everything this needs from Foundations and Calculus 1. I’ll work the first example with you, and the guided steps are there whenever you want them.

copy.firstVisit: The outpost has stopped just storing things and started moving them: sleds, cranes, catapults, flywheels. Every one of them obeys a handful of rules, and by the end you will be able to predict where any of them will be. We start with something humble: agreeing on units.
copy.allDone: Every machine on the ridge now runs on your numbers. Next, the ripples they make: Waves.
copy.chaptersNote: Seven chapters. Learn every concept in a chapter to unlock a landmark for the outpost. Practice missions are optional.

skills.title: The skill tree
skills.text: Follow the prerequisite branches from units and vectors to rotation and orbits. Each mission you finish opens the ideas that are built on it.

visual.title: The concept bench
visual.text: Pick any mission, change its numbers and predict the result before you check it. Nothing here affects your progress, and it all works offline.

help.title: Look for the rule behind the motion.
help.intro: Mechanics starts from a few laws: how things are measured, how they move, what pushes them, and which quantities they keep. Every new word and symbol is explained before you are asked to use it, with a worked example first. Angles are always in radians.
help.answers: Answers are numbers in SI units (metres, seconds, kilograms, newtons) or a named prefix, typed without commas or spaces. Every prompt names the unit of each answer box. Signs matter: a velocity of −3 m/s is typed as -3.
